newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Long-term NZ economic growth at risk - ManFed.
newsitem.headline: Long-term NZ economic growth at risk - ManFed.

text.p: New Zealand is in danger of returning to short-term stimulation of the domestic economy at the expense of long-term sustainable and export-led growth, the Manufacturers Federation said on Thursday.

"Increased spending by the coalition government, particularly in 1998/9 and the following year, will stimulate the domestic economy and fuel the very areas causing our current inflation," ManFed chief executive officer Simon Arnold said.
The conservative National Party and centrist New Zealand First formed a coalition government last month.
Arnold said exporters would continue to face an overvalued exchange rate unless the government found savings that would compensate for higher government spending.
Compulsory savings schemes would do little to help because they were unlikely to increase the overall level of savings.

"Increased government spending at a time when households are borrowing heavily will therefore hurt our export sector. Higher spending does give a push to domestic growth, but this will not last long."
Arnold said the high New Zealand dollar would see reduced investment in the export sector, a further fall in exports, lost jobs and a rising current account deficit.
Business closures and job losses in the export sector would soon see more cautious household spending, which would take the edge off inflation.
"But with better economic management these sorts of risks could be reduced. Better quality expenditure, timed to reduce inflationary pressure, is still possible," Arnold said.
